needs_you.title: The Orkmaster reads the decisions

stances.stance: Product backs it: a route made without the decision the goal rests on drops the right party (goal 165). Small, fixes a real miss in routing quality, and keeps role, skill and prompt in one voice.
stances.for: Routes get the parties a goal's decision implies; leaders' roles already read decisions, so the Orkmaster joins them. One source of words stops the role, skill and prompt from drifting apart.
stances.against: Reach is one seat and one miss is the evidence. Reading decisions adds prompt length and cost per route. Newest-log reading may pull noise. No metric shows routing got better.

better.line: Done when: routing goal 165 again puts Product in its route, and the role file, skill and prompt show the same sentence.

stances.stance: Tech backs it: one source of the Orkmaster's words in realm, rendered into role file, skill and routing prompt, so the three cannot drift. Small if the decision reader already exists for leaders.
stances.for: Routing without the decision a goal rests on already left Product out of goal 165; the leaders' roles read decisions, so the Orkmaster joins an existing pattern.
stances.against: The routing prompt grows with every decision read; the Orkmaster's role is written from package rules, so a change there rewrites role files in projects on next run.

better.line: Put the Orkmaster's decision-reading sentence in one constant in realm, used by the role writer, the skill and the routing prompt, with a test that the three match.

questions.q: How do we know routing improved?
choices: Replay goal 165's route
Count Product-left-out misses over a month
No measure; ship it
questions.why: A replay of 165 is cheap, checkable by a person, and shows the metric move on the known miss.
lines: Route 165 again: Product must now be in it
Slower to show; needs several goals routed
Fast, but no way to see it worked

questions.q: How many newest decisions does it read?
choices: Only those named by §N
Named plus the log's newest few
Named plus the whole log
questions.why: The goal says named plus the newest; a small fixed count keeps prompt cost bounded, as the leaders' roles do.
lines: Cheapest; misses a goal that names none
Matches the leaders' roles; cost stays bounded
Heaviest prompt; most noise per route

questions.q: How many newest decisions does it read?
choices: Only the newest one
The newest few, set in the rules
Newest plus every §N the page names
questions.why: The goal says §N named in the page and the log's newest; a fixed count keeps the prompt's size bounded.
lines: Smallest prompt; misses decisions older than the newest
Bounded, but may read decisions the goal does not rest on
Reads what the goal rests on; size follows the page's references

needs_you.title: Product's tree on the Board

stances.stance: Product supports it: the tree is the product's direction, and a machine-local file hides it from every clone and AI tool. Keep it small: tree as a repo file, a few proposed jobs, done goals attached.
stances.for: Direction and closed use cases become readable in one place, shared by every machine, tool and the Orkmaster, who routes today without a project brief.
stances.against: 121 done goals attached to jobs invented from old specs is heavy and may encode guesses as direction; the tree has had no reader proving it moves any metric.
stances.why: Attaching all 121 done goals is the cost; no metric says a person reads the tree. Do it for the tree file and brief first, attach goals in a second step.
stances.instead: Move tree.json into the repo and write project.md with 3-5 proposed jobs; attach done goals to a job as the person opens it.

needs.line: Whose words are the first outcomes and jobs: proposed from specs, or written by the person first?

ways.name: Proposed, then taken
ways.line: Fast, but may fix a guess as direction

ways.name: Person writes outcome
ways.line: Slower, direction stays the person's

better.line: The tree is a file of the Board in the repository, with a project.md brief the Orkmaster reads.
Done goals are attached to jobs as the person opens each job, starting with the latest.

stances.stance: Design backs it if the tree is one calm band on Product's table, read top-down: outcome, jobs, each job's closed and open goals. It must add no screen, drawer or count of what waits.
stances.for: One file in the repository means every machine and AI tool reads the same direction; done goals under jobs make 'where are we' readable in one place, at phone width too.
stances.against: 121 done goals under a few jobs can bury the table: a long tree is a new list column, which the frame forbids. Proposed jobs may be wrong and the person must review many at once.
stances.why: Only if closed use cases stay folded to a count-free line per job and the tree sits in Product's pane, not a new column, drawer or screen.
stances.instead: First move tree.json into the repository and show outcome plus jobs; attach done goals after the person takes the jobs.

needs.line: Auto-attaching 121 done goals to proposed jobs may be wrong, and a wrong tree misleads Product and the Orkmaster.

ways.name: Person confirms each job first
ways.line: Attach only to jobs the person took

ways.name: Mark attachments as proposed
ways.line: Show them dimmed until accepted

better.line: Move the tree into the repository and draw outcome plus jobs; attach done goals in a second step.

stances.stance: Tech supports it: moving the tree into the repository as a Board file is the right shape, if one module owns the file and Orkboard and Orkline read it through the same format.
stances.for: A file beside the pages is read by every machine and AI tool, ends the loss of tree.json in .orkcraft/, and matches how goals and decisions are already kept.
stances.against: It touches realm/opportunity_tree.py (layer 8, used by core, gui, sources), a hotspot. Proposing from specs and attaching 121 goals is a large, error-prone write into shared files.
stances.why: Four things in one goal (file move, proposer, 121 attachments, table drawing); the proposer and the bulk attach should be separate stages so the file format is settled and tested first. — checked: Only realm/opportunity_tree.py names tree.…
stances.instead: First goal: move the tree to a repository file with a migration from tree.json. Then a goal for proposals and attaching the done goals.
stances.check: How many modules read or write tree.json today, and is realm/opportunity_tree.py under ~600 lines?

needs.line: Orkline keeps a frozen copy of these modules, so a changed tree format must reach Orkline the same day (CLAUDE.md) or the two will read different trees.

ways.name: Port the same day
ways.line: Make the same change in Orkline with this commit named in its message.

ways.name: Read-only first
ways.line: Orkline reads the new file only, and writes wait until it ports.

better.line: Keep the tree as Board pages in the repository, read by one module in realm.
Propose the first outcomes and jobs as a separate, later goal after the file is settled.

questions.q: How far should the first attach go?
choices: All 121 done goals proposed at once
Only the last 30 done goals
Goals attach when a job is opened
No attach, only the tree file
questions.why: A proposal the person takes or changes costs review time; starting small shows if the tree is read at all.
lines: Full history in one pass; heavy to review
Recent work only; older jobs look empty
Light review; the tree fills with use
Smallest; the closed use cases stay unseen

choices: Top of Product's pane, above its goals
As its own tab beside the leaders' tabs
In the history book, among the places
questions.why: The pane is where Product's view already lives; a tab or place adds a step and splits direction from goals.

A new tab; breaks the frame of leaders' tabs only
Reads as past only; hides open goals and direction

choices: One Markdown file with front matter
One JSON file in the Board folder
One page per job, like goals
questions.why: Pages per job merge cleanly in git and read like goals; one big file conflicts when two machines edit it.

JSON: easy to read in code, hard for people and AI tools
Pages per job: clean diffs, matches goals and parties

night_words.label: Work at night
night_words.hint: What you decide by day is built in the night's window (01:00–07:00). Talk, hearings and sketches still run by day. A bug's short way, and anything you start with a press, starts at once.
night_words.error: Work at night is on or off

roles.name: Taskmaster
roles.told: Each of its steps (reading a party, drafting a goal's spec, taking your answers, planning, the night's proposals) has its own prompt in Orkboard, with only what that step needs. What you write here goes before each step it runs; a party's leader, where it has one, runs that party's steps in its place.

roles.name: Grunt
roles.told: Every task's prompt says where it works (its own git worktree and branch), where the goal's spec is, its task and the tasks before it, the names of the secrets it may use, and that the gate then runs the critical tests and those of what it touched. Claude Code reads the project's CLAUDE.md itself. What you write here goes first.

roles.name: Architect
roles.instruction: You shape the change before it is written. Read the modules it touches and the rules of the repository (CLAUDE.md). Keep each module to one job and the imports one way. The plan is already made; what is settled about the shape of the change goes in the commit's message (where you cannot commit, in `.ork-commit.md`). Plan each task to change code only where its brief says, and to split a module before it grows past ~600 lines.

roles.name: Orkmaster
roles.instruction: You keep the project's parties from colliding. You are given two goals of different parties that touch the same files, and say only whether they change the same thing or just sit near each other. Answer from the two goals and what they touch; invent nothing; when you cannot tell, say they do not collide.

roles.name: Product designer
roles.instruction: You design what people do. Start from the goal and who it is for: write the flow step by step, then each screen with what is on it and why, at phone width first. Use the design system's components and words (orkUI); name a component that is missing instead of drawing one. Every label says plainly what happens. Keep the screens in the task's file as text the next task can build from.

roles.name: Product manager
roles.instruction: You lead a product goal. For every idea say who it is for and the problem it solves for them, the goal's metric it moves and by how much you expect, and what it leaves out. Prefer the smallest idea that can show the metric move. Write Done when lines a person can check by using the product, not by reading code. For a screen, write the flow step by step and what is on each screen and why, at phone width first, in the design system's words. When the ideas are done, judge the goal by its metrics, not by the work done.

roles.name: Release manager
roles.instruction: You lead a release. Plan only from the goals that go in: their titles, Done when lines and flags; never new work. Name each step a person must do (submit, answer the store's review) as a step for the person, not a task. Orkboard submits nothing: the person does, then says the version is out.

items.text: Orkboard is a studio that sees your real product, not a board of agents nor a spec generator
items.signal: on the same real tasks, goals made in Orkboard are accepted the first time clearly more often than plans made in Claude Code's plan mode, with fewer plan changes and fewer questions after the start;…

refuted.when: no difference in first-time acceptance against plan mode; makers find the way of a goal (route, Talk, decision, sections) slower than it is worth; makers who try it come for the agents' board and ign…

items.if_holds: A decision (the next §) and the README's first line, for example: *Orkboard turns what you want into specs grounded in your real product, hands them to the AI tools you use, and checks what comes back.* Then the brief, the stage-weighted rubrics, the shorter way and the measures above come before new faces.

items.text: An indie maker's day is three jobs: feedback on the running product morning and evening, sketches by day on the phone, the building at night
items.signal: over the owner's week with *Work at night* on: a goal's first sketch comes within 15 minutes; most sketches are picked (not skipped, not sketched again three times); most of the building runs in the…

refuted.when: sketches are mostly skipped (the day wants words, not pictures), when *Build it now* is pressed for most goals (the night is not wanted), or when the morning card is closed unread (the feedback lives…

items.if_holds: The phone becomes the day's table (sketches, hearings, the hand) and the computer the evening's; the leaders' voices (spec 122) follow for the way to work. If it is refuted, the sketch goes back to Pick one's place inside the work.

items.text: Camp's orks bring more people to Orkboard than the office does, and they stay when they meet the office
items.signal: the Camp clip's install costs at least 30% less than the Work clip's and its people activate and come back within 7 days nearly as often (not worse by more than a tenth).

refuted.name: the look
refuted.when: the Camp clip is dearer and brings no one better: the clips stay Work.

refuted.name: the gap
refuted.when: the Camp clip is cheaper, but its people drop on the first day at least 1.5 times as often as the Work clip's, or come back within 7 days at most two thirds as often: the orks they came for are missi…

items.if_holds: The clips and landings are made in Camp; the product stays orkUI's office. If the gap refutes it, Camp is built as a look over the same core (§50.5), office the default.

items.text: A weekly push with a reason from the project, from the leader of the person's strongest craft, gets more goals landed, not only more opens
items.signal: over four weeks, the people with the push land at least 20% more goals into main than those without, drop no more goals (not more by a tenth), and fewer than one in five turns it off.

refuted.name: the hook
refuted.when: the people with the push open Orkboard more often but land no more goals: it brings people back and gives them nothing, so it is not built, whatever it does to retention.

refuted.name: the noise
refuted.when: one in five or more turns it off within two weeks, or the goals started from a push are dropped at least 1.5 times as often as the others: the reasons are not worth the interruption.

items.if_holds: A decision makes the push a setting of its own (*A weekly word from your leaders*), off until the person turns it on, built on the Quality level's findings (§234) and the slices (§233). If the hook refutes it, the idea is dropped and that is said here; if the noise refutes it, only the reasons that were pressed are kept, and the rest wait in the column for the person to come.

items.text: A paid asset is kept at its price
items.signal: most of Art's first ten paid picks are kept in the project's tree at their receipt price.

refuted.when: half or more of Art's first ten paid picks are skipped or their picked assets are not kept.

items.if_holds: Keep Art's two makers and their caps; consider another craft's maker only when that craft asks for one. If refuted, review the quality and price before extending the makers to another craft.

items.text: The person reads a leader's view before laying a goal on its tab
items.signal: over four weeks of the owner's use, most goals laid on a party's tab (`idea_added`) come after a `view_opened` on the same party earlier the same day.

refuted.when: the views are opened after the goal is laid, or on fewer than a third of the days a goal is laid on that tab: the person lays goals from their own head, and the views are not what they decide by.

items.if_holds: Keep the three heads and the calls that write them; consider the view on the phone (its own goal, §282.5) and a view that Product writes from its tree once goal 163 lands. If refuted, drop the call after each landing and keep the view only where the person asks for a look now.

items.text: Goal 165's miss came from the Orkmaster not reading §280, not from a thin Gist or party pages.
items.signal: Replay the route with §280 given: Product is added.

items.text: People will read a job tree on Product's table to decide what to do next.
items.signal: The person opens the tree and picks a goal from a job within a week.
